taxonomy_note: Workflow routing only. Choose final root-cause taxonomy from supported evidence.

controls.boundary: Device Authorization Grant account/device transaction binding
controls.source_trace: Separate the device transaction, user confirmation and polling client. Determine which account and audience the final token represents, including user-visible confirmation.
controls.implementation_branch: Distinguish device_code, human user_code and the polling client; they have different audiences. A user confirmation must be tied to the intended device transaction, but cross-device confirmation is normal. Use expiry/polling errors as protocol observations, not evidence of account authentication unless a token is actually issued.
controls.operational_method: Identify issuer, client_id, device_code and the approved user transaction in the polling state. Public clients are identified differently from confidential clients that authenticate. Separate authorization_pending, access_denied and expired_token states from successful token issuance; a user_code displayed on another device is normal. Compare rightful polling with a client/transaction mismatch in an owned issuer fixture, without asking a real user to approve an attacker transaction.
controls.controlled_verification: In an owned issuer fixture confirm one device transaction, then compare another client/device transaction and expired/reused codes without guessing user codes.
controls.false_positive_discriminator: A deliberately portable user code is not a flaw by itself; no token issuance or wrong-account binding means the strong claim is unproved.
controls.remediation_acceptance: Bind the approved transaction, client and account; retest legitimate pairing, expiry and unauthorized transaction substitution.
